data.body:
Pilot cutover design (settled before implementation):

Classification of the 3 legacy reads (all owner=composition per the gate — load_config, and os.environ.get with a DYNAMIC config-supplied env name → 'unresolved-env-read'):
- mcp_server.py L422 (_mcp_gate), L591 (build_server cfg-None fallback), L735 (main): load_config() per-call/below-seam.
- mcp_server.py L646: os.environ.get(mcp_cfg.auth_proxy_secret_env) — proxy secret at HTTP app-wrap time.
- _mcp_auth.py L411 (introspection client_secret_env), L658 (build_composite_verifier proxy secret), L760 (_parse_static_record token_env): startup-time auth SECRET resolutions by config-named env var.

Rejected: the '# read-via:' marker — precedent (only in _config_schema.py, 12x) is documenting a config FIELD's read site, NOT suppressing consumer env reads. Not the intended owned-registration mechanism here.

Rejected: adding _mcp_auth.py to the gate's credential-boundary set — the reads classify as composition (unresolved dynamic name), not credential, so boundary ownership would not suppress them.

Chosen: genuine cut-to-seam. (1) Compose MCP config ONCE at server startup (main→build_server) and bind it so _mcp_gate/_readonly read the startup-bound value instead of load_config() per request. (2) Resolve the auth secret VALUES at that same startup composition (the boundary allowed to read env) and thread the resolved values into build_composite_verifier / the proxy-app wrap / static-token parsing, so _mcp_auth.py and mcp_server.py L646 no longer call os.environ.get. Then remove all 3 LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS entries; the gate (scan root src/rebar) must be clean. Behavioral oracle: tests/interfaces/facades MCP+auth suites + tests/interfaces/contracts MCP envelope + tests/unit/test_mcp_writes.py/test_mcp_plan_review_status.py (178 passing baseline; test_mcp_push_status.py excluded — pre-existing git-hooks env fixture flake, unrelated). Held-out seam-clean proof: tests/scripts/test_mcp_server_seam_clean_heldout.py.
